meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-14 | Start: 10:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood), Samir Dutta (Redwood SE), Talia Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Cerebro ML), Omar Nazir (Cerebro Infra), Priya Singh (Cerebro PM)
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on reducing time-to-first-token (TTFT) and streaming behaviour for Cerebro's retrieval-augmented generation workload. Reviewed last week's benchmarks (mixed results), debated kernel selection tradeoffs for medium-long sequences, agreed to run kernel A/B with continuous batching and provide production prompt samples. Next steps center on targeted traces, cost delta, and a follow-up run next week.
topics: Streaming vs batch tradeoffs for interactive use cases
Sequence length distribution impact on kernel pathing
Kernel A vs Kernel B (float16 quant / fused attention)
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm gonna kick us off. we have about 50 minutes. Samir and Talia from Redwood, and Rachel, Omar, Priya from Cerebro. quick goal — sync on last week's TTFT runs and align next experiments.
[00:18] Rachel Kim: thanks Lena. quick note, we saw some flakiness in the initial experiment, some runs had huge jitter. i pulled the traces but i haven't shared them yet — will do after this call.
[00:28] Samir Dutta: yeah the jitter's what we saw too; i think some of that was warmup cus the first few tokens hit different kernel tails. for clarity — are you using streaming in prod or firing full generation?
[00:37] Priya Singh: mostly streaming for the UI, users expect quick first token then stream. some batch background jobs do full generation but that's not the interactive path.
[00:47] Talia Ortiz: ok that helps, streaming constraints mean we need to prioritize TTFT not just throughput. we also need to know your seq length distribution, even 1-2% of long sequences will skew kernel choices.
[00:58] Omar Nazir: i have the histogram locally — majority around 512 but a tail to 3k. i'll export and share. the UI also pre-sends prefixes from the session context so effective seq often hits 800-1200.
[01:12] Samir Dutta: perfect — that tail explains why Kernel B (the fused-attn path) sometimes underperformed on median. Kernel A is better at < 768 usually. Kernel B gives better throughput at high seq but added startup overhead.
[01:27] Rachel Kim: can you remind me which kernel is enabled by default in the pilot image? we thought we were on B.
[01:33] Lena Park: right now pilot nodes were on Kernel B to maximize gross throughput. we can flip profiles per node pool though.
[01:40] Priya Singh: our main ask is lower TTFT for interactive — if flipping causes a small throughput hit but big TTFT improvement, that could be fine. we care about p50/p90 for first token.
[01:52] Samir Dutta: that tradeoff is expected. two knobs: kernel choice and batching policy. continuous-batching reduces per-token overhead for long tails but can increase first-token latency for ultra-low payloads unless prewarm or small-batch prioritization is enabled.
[02:07] Talia Ortiz: also quantization profile matters — we tested an aggressive int4 run that cut cost ~30% but added +40ms to first token in some cases due to extra dequant steps in the path.
[02:19] Omar Nazir: hmm we actually considered int8 for cost, but int4 noises me. is there any fallback automatic path if quantized variant misses quality?
[02:27] Samir Dutta: yes — Redwood runtime allows automatic fallback to float16 variant on quality regressions or if warmup triggers; that's part of the rollout policy. but fallback can add latency if it happens mid-request.
[02:38] Rachel Kim: last week's run numbers — i saw p50 TTFT 80ms then some runs 300ms. how confident are you those were kernel-related vs networking?
[02:48] Samir Dutta: we looked at traces — many long TTFT events correlate with kernel selection and cold kv-cache populating. a few were also network retries on the customer side when clients re-opened sockets.
[03:01] Lena Park: note we pushed a small client-side keepalive change last week which should reduce socket churn, that might help your scatter.
[03:09] Priya Singh: good. on the benchmarking side, will you run continuous-batching vs classic windowed batching?
[03:15] Samir Dutta: yes plan is to run both with the same payload set. continuous-batching gives better aggregate tokens/sec but can add 10-35ms to TTFT on small single-turn prompts unless we tune prioritization. we can also try prefix-cache warmup for common prefixes.
[03:29] Rachel Kim: when you say prioritization, is that per-token priority or per-request? we need first token prioritized over bulk background jobs.
[03:36] Talia Ortiz: we can set request-level priority so interactive routes get a smaller batch target and more aggressive scheduling. that's what we'll test.
[03:44] Omar Nazir: about KV/prefix cache — we saw cold-cache TTFT spikes. can Redwood persist KV cache across requests for the same session?
[03:52] Samir Dutta: yes, in Dedicated and Private you can persist session KV cache in memory-local to a worker and reuse it. on hosted we do ephemeral caches but you can enable sticky routing to reuse the same worker for a session to reduce cold-cache incidence.
[04:05] Priya Singh: sticky routing might be okay, but what about scaling — if a worker goes down then you lose the cache. what are tradeoffs?
[04:13] Samir Dutta: exactly — sticky helps TTFT dramatically for sessions but hurts elasticity. fallback policies can route to a compatible worker and we can warmup the KV cache with the last n tokens stored in redis; there's a tradeoff on cost and complexity.
[04:27] Lena Park: ok practical experiment plan: run kernel A and kernel B on identical node types with two batching configs: continuous-batching tuned for interactive priority, and conventional batching at 50ms window. measure p50/p90 TTFT, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1M tokens.
[04:42] Rachel Kim: sounds good. can you also include a run with sticky routing enabled? smells helpful for our session-based flows.
[04:48] Samir Dutta: yes we'll include sticky routing + warmup heuristic.
[04:52] Priya Singh: and please try a small int8 quant run as a middle ground — int4 seemed risky but int8 might be OK.
[04:59] Talia Ortiz: agreed — small int8 profile included. we'll also capture raw kernel invocation timestamps to see where the delta is.
[05:07] Omar Nazir: re: metrics — what do you need from our side? i can share the prompt corpus and a histogram of seq lengths.
[05:13] Lena Park: please provide: a) 50 representative prompts b) seq length histogram c) any sharp SLA requirements for p50/p90 TTFT and max cost per 1k tokens.
[05:24] Rachel Kim: i'll compile the prompts and send them to Samir; they include a fair amount of long context because of the retrieval chains.
[05:31] Samir Dutta: perfect. i also want to call out noise sources — client-side socket churn, webapp batching of user input, and the RAG retrieval latency. we should probably separate retrieval time from model TTFT, is that possible?
[05:43] Omar Nazir: yes retrieval is measured separately in our logs. we'll provide a timeline mapping retrieval vs request arrival so you can isolate model time.
[05:51] Priya Singh: what about regression detection — we need an automated check so we don't push a config that regresses p50.
[05:57] Talia Ortiz: Redwood Optimize can run evals on a small set of prompts and alert on quality drops; for TTFT we can add a gated metric in the rollout policy to block a variant if p50 gets worse than x% versus baseline.
[06:10] Rachel Kim: can that gate be tied to a canary? like only 5% traffic and then halt?
[06:15] Samir Dutta: yes — canary + automatic rollback is possible.
[06:18] Lena Park: ok to summarize: we run kernel A/B + batching modes + sticky, include int8 trial. Samir will upload traces and raw kernel timestamps. Cerebro will send 50 prompts and seq histograms. Redwood will produce a tab with cost delta and expected p50/p90 impact.
[06:36] Rachel Kim: any security or compliance asks? we are evaluating for regulated customers.
[06:41] Lena Park: we will share SOC2 and ISO artifacts and a short note on how KV cache persistence options affect residency and logs. i'll email the docs.
[06:51] Priya Singh: timeline — when can we expect the runs?
[06:55] Samir Dutta: i can start runs tomorrow, want a 48hr window to collect stable numbers and then we analyze. so deliverables by 2026-05-19.
[07:04] Omar Nazir: that works. can you also include cost-per-hour estimates for sticky routing scenarios?
[07:09] Samir Dutta: yep will include cost modeling.
[07:12] Lena Park: great. last bit — next meeting same time next week? May 21st?
[07:16] Priya Singh: yes that's fine.
[07:18] Lena Park: perfect. thanks all. minutes and action items will be sent.
[07:24] (call ends)
